page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highcpu-8 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance featuring 8 vCPUs and 16 GB of RAM, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. The instance is powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8581C processor operating at 2.3 GHz, configured with 4 physical cores and 2 threads per core. The CPU architecture is x86_64, supported by a 260 MB L3 cache. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core performance, with Geekbench single-core and text processing scores placing in the top 10% tier. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also show strong performance in the top 25% tier. Multi-core operations, including stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and software compilation, fall within the average range. Memory bandwidth is measured at 70.65 GB/sec for large block read-only operations and 40.19 GB/sec for large block write operations.

The c4-highcpu-8 offers high single-thread execution efficiency, making it cost-effective for workloads that do not require massive memory footprints or local storage. However, the 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU represents a tradeoff for memory-intensive applications. Additionally, LLM inference performance drops to the bottom 25% tier for text generation on medium 7B models, and large 70B models are unsupported due to memory constraints.

This instance is suitable for compute-bound tasks such as text processing, single-threaded data compression, software compilation, and static web serving. It is also applicable for lightweight database operations and small-scale language model prompt processing.
